title: Zanzibar Seafood Linguine
localName: Pasta ya Vyakula vya Bahari — Zanzibar
community: Zanzibar hotel cuisine — the Indian Ocean's answer to Italian pasta
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Seafood Linguine — linguine tossed with Zanzibar prawns, octopus, and clams in a coconut milk, tamarind, and Zanzibar spice sauce with fresh tomatoes and coriander. Italian pasta elevated by the full power of the Indian Ocean — Zanzibar's hotel restaurants at their finest.
longDesc: Zanzibar seafood linguine is the dish that Zanzibar's finest hotels invented to bridge the preferences of international guests with the extraordinary quality of Indian Ocean seafood. The coconut-tamarind sauce is pure Zanzibar; the pasta is the universal medium that makes it accessible to everyone. The result is one of the most sophisticated dishes in Tanzania's modern culinary repertoire.
ingredients: 150g small octopus or squid — cleaned and sliced
steps: Cook linguine in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan. Sauté shallots and garlic until soft — 3 minutes.
Add cumin, cardamom, and chilli flakes. Stir 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes and tamarind. Cook 5 minutes until reduced.
Pour in coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add clams or mussels first. Cover 2 minutes until they open.
Add prawns. Cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add drained linguine. Toss to coat. Add pasta water if needed.
Finish with lime zest, lime juice, and coriander.
chefTips: Reserve pasta water — the starch thickens and binds the sauce beautifully.
Add seafood in order of cooking time — clams first, prawns second, squid last.
Al dente pasta is essential — it finishes cooking in the sauce.
The cardamom is the Zanzibar signature — do not omit.
commonMistakes: Fully-cooked pasta before adding to sauce — becomes mushy.
cookingScience: Pasta water contains dissolved starch — when added to the sauce, this starch further thickens and emulsifies the coconut milk sauce, helping it coat the linguine uniformly. The final lime juice acid addition brightens all flavours and partially denatures surface proteins on the seafood, creating a subtle flavour enhancement.
sustainabilityTips: Zanzibar Indian Ocean seafood from local fishermen — the shortest possible food chain.
servedWith: Zanzibar white wine equivalent — cold ginger lemonade (TZA239)
reheating: Very gently with a splash of coconut milk.
healthBenefits: High lean protein from multiple seafood sources.
culturalNote: Zanzibar seafood linguine is what happens when the finest Italian pasta technique meets the Indian Ocean's greatest seafood and the Swahili spice tradition — a dish that could only exist in Zanzibar, that could only have been invented where these three food worlds collide.
